notes: The syscall instruction clobbers rcx (the return address lands in rcx) and r11 (the flags land in r11).

Since Linux 5.14 the kernel reads the syscall number from eax and ignores the upper 32 bits of rax. Older kernels fail with ENOSYS when those bits are not zero, and mov eax, N clears them, so it works on both.
